question.text: The risk that a derivative contract may not be legally enforceable is known as:

explanation.text: The Logic: Legal or regulatory risk concerns the enforceability of contracts, including derivative contracts. Operational risk, by contrast, covers items such as failures in systems, processes, and inadequate documentation. Model risk relates to errors in pricing models, and credit risk is about counterparty default. The Trap: Inadequate documentation belongs under operational risk in the source, not under legal risk; only enforceability of the contract itself is grouped under legal or regulatory risk. Note: Page 17 supports the legal/regulatory and operational risk categorisations used above; no source-backed claim is made here that the SCRA amendment was specifically introduced to address legal risk.
